architecture_under_test: Public money → Citizen allocation → Independent journalism
analogy_warning: Seattle Democracy Vouchers are campaign-finance evidence for allocation mechanics/participation patterns — NOT evidence that journalism vouchers work.

failure_modes.name: Popularity contest
failure_modes.evidence: Predicted by voucher literature; no US journalism voucher pilot to observe

failure_modes.name: Partisan mobilization
failure_modes.evidence: Campaign vouchers show organized uptake; journalism transfer untested

failure_modes.name: Celebrity / large outlets dominate
failure_modes.evidence: Proposals often add caps (e.g., 1% caps in academic designs) precisely because of this risk

failure_modes.name: Fraud / bot identities
failure_modes.evidence: Administrative identity problem acknowledged in policy menus; not empirically measured for news vouchers

failure_modes.name: Sensationalism incentives
failure_modes.evidence: Attention markets; infrastructure-floor hypothesis responds to this

failure_modes.name: Low-information allocation
failure_modes.evidence: Citizens may not know which outlets cover quorum courts

failure_modes.name: Rich communities supplement more
failure_modes.evidence: Tax-credit designs especially regressive; voucher designs claim mitigation — untested for news

failure_modes.name: Rural outlets lack scale / compliance capacity
failure_modes.evidence: Arkansas pilot shows small rural papers; admin burden risk high

not_usable_for: proof that news vouchers increase institutional journalism
